items.stem: An 'async-first' team treats which approach as the default?

options.text: Real-time video calls for every discussion
options.rationale: That is sync-first and scales poorly across time zones.

options.text: Written, documented communication that others read on their own schedule
options.rationale: Correct: async-first defaults to durable writing, reserving sync for what truly needs it.
Expecting instant replies recreates always-on pressure, not async work.
Async-first depends on strong written records.

items.explanation: Correct: async-first defaults to durable writing, reserving sync for what truly needs it.

items.stem: The healthiest way to manage a remote report's performance is to focus on:

options.text: Hours shown as active in the chat tool
options.rationale: Activity signals measure presence, not value, and invite gaming.

options.text: The outcomes and deliverables they are accountable for
options.rationale: Correct: managing by outcomes respects autonomy and measures real results.
Response speed is not a measure of meaningful output.
Surveillance erodes trust without improving results.

items.explanation: Correct: managing by outcomes respects autonomy and measures real results.

items.stem: Which TWO steps reduce proximity bias on a hybrid team? (Select TWO)

options.text: Make sure remote members get the same access to informal information and sponsors
options.rationale: Correct: equal access counters the in-office information advantage.

options.text: Base recognition and promotion on documented outcomes, not visibility
options.rationale: Correct: outcome-based decisions reduce bias toward whoever is seen most.

options.text: Favour in-office staff for stretch projects because they are easier to reach
options.rationale: That is exactly the proximity bias to avoid.

options.text: Hold key conversations in the hallway where only on-site staff hear them
options.rationale: Hallway decisions exclude remote colleagues and entrench bias.

items.explanation: Correct: equal access counters the in-office information advantage.; Correct: outcome-based decisions reduce bias toward whoever is seen most.
